# s227 — Finish implementation with handoff so done is recorded only after landing

Set this project's `implement_finish` to `handoff`, so an implementing agent ends with `handoff` and `done` is recorded on `main` only after review and merge.

**Findings:** done-audit 2026-10-05: agents marked s220 and s225 done in worktrees before merge; both were set back by hand · **Size:** S · **Tree:** docs

**Not in this slice:** changing slicer's default (`done`), changing the `handoff`, `reject`, `done` or `next --status review` commands or their JSON, adding a `config set` command, adding enforcement that refuses `done` before a merge, or changing any other project's config.

## Why

This project's config has `implement_finish` set to `done`, so the documented loop ends with `done` in the implementation worktree, before anything is merged. On 2026-10-05 the log shows it twice: s220 was marked done at 12:57Z and set back to started at 12:59Z, and s225 was marked done at 16:37Z and set back at 16:45Z. Both were then handed off to review and marked done after landing.

`main` never carried either early done, because tracking state reaches `main` only through commits. A worktree's own `list` and `status` did say done while the work was unmerged. An audit of all 192 done items found every one merged into `main`, and no unmerged branches or worktrees. So the cost has been manual corrections, not lost work.

With `handoff`, the implementer's finish is the review status. The reviewer picks it up with `slicer next --status review --start`, lands it, and runs `done` on `main`. That is how s220, s225 and s190 were landed in practice.

## Files

- `.slicer/config.json`, the single key `implement_finish`
- `AGENTS.md` (the pickup/implement block and "Landing a slice")
- `tests/test_ai.py` (the roadmap-section size limit only, and only if the rewrite cannot fit)

## Failing tests

1. `slicer config implement_finish` prints `handoff`, and `slicer config review_status` is non-empty, which handoff mode requires.
2. `slicer ai instructions` in this repo ends step 4 with `slicer handoff ID --render --check` and does not carry the `done` command.
3. `AGENTS.md` tells the implementer to finish with `slicer handoff <ID> ... --render --check` and not to run `done`. Its "Landing a slice" tells the reviewer to pick up with `next --status review --start --ready --section "Check"`, review, commit, merge with `git merge --no-ff`, run `slicer done <ID> --note ... --render --check` on `main`, commit that, then remove the worktree and branch.
4. The `test_ai.py` assertions on `AGENTS.md` still pass: the CLI-only sentence, the `next --ready` pickup command, `slicer start <ID> --render --strict`, the `edit S07 ... --render --strict` example, and the `done <ID>` line. The roadmap-section limit of 3,800 bytes also still holds. It was 3,797 bytes at `a2bb617`, so the rewrite must shorten other text, or raise the limit with a stated reason.
5. A throwaway item run end to end: after `handoff` in its worktree, the worktree shows `review`, `main`'s `list` shows `wt:NAME`, and `main` shows done only after the merge and `done` there. `slicer check` passes at each step.

## Implement

This slice carries one explicit owner exception. `slicer config` is read-only and no command writes the config, while `AGENTS.md` forbids hand-editing `.slicer/*.json`. So edit that one key in `.slicer/config.json` and nothing else, then run `slicer check`. If the owner would rather not make the exception, file a `config set` item first and make this one depend on it.

Then rewrite the finish steps in `AGENTS.md` to the handoff loop above. Keep what `test_ai.py` asserts, and keep the section under its byte limit.

Confirm the shipped skill still reads correctly: its step 4 already says to run `handoff` instead of `done` when `implement_finish` is `handoff`, so no change is expected. Say in the note whether it needed one. No CHANGELOG entry: this changes this project's process, not the product.

Items already started in worktrees when the switch lands finish with `handoff` too. Do not run `done` on a worktree branch.
